chunks: 63 - What Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has angels whom He has entrusted with the vegetation of the earth, among the trees and the palm trees. There is no tree and no palm tree except that with it there is, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, an angel guarding it and what belongs to it. Were it not that with it there is one who protects it, the beasts and the creeping creatures of the earth would consume it when its fruit is in it.

key_terms.بِنَبَاتِ الْأَرْضِ: the vegetation and plant growth of the earth
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةً: angels appointed by Allah for a specific task
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel assigned as a guardian
key_terms.هَوَامُّ الْأَرْضِ: creeping creatures and pests of the earth

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Allah’s protection of trees and their fruits?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, has appointed angels over the vegetation of the earth, especially trees and palm trees, to guard them. It highlights divine care and unseen governance in the natural world, showing that the preservation of provision is by Allah's command through His mala'ikah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.63 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, has appointed angels to protect the vegetation of the earth, including trees and palm trees. There is no tree or palm except that there is an angel with it from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, who guards it. If it were not for the presence of those angels to protect them, wild animals and pests would consume their fruits."
